newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline up with NYMEX Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline up with NYMEX Friday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline prices edged higher Friday, in sympathy with higher paper markets, while traders looked toward a quiet market next week as most attended an industry conference.
Prices moved up Friday with futures contracts on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), with heating oil rising 0.14 cent a gallon. June NYMEX unleaded gasoline firmed 0.39 cents a gallon.
++ Gasoline. Conventional grade unleaded gasoline rose 0.50 cent a gallon from Thursday to 60.50/61.50 cents in Los Angeles, with San Francisco grades talked 1.25 cents lower.
Prompt CARB gasoline ranged 63.50/64.50 cents a gallon, with June shipments values one cent higher.
Bids for CARB unleaded gasoline also gained half a cent, with traders pegging offers at 64.50 cent and bids at 63.50 cents.

The California Energy Commission's weekly gasoline report, published May 8, showed state CARB inventories at an adequate 4.4 million barrels for the week ended May 2, compared to about 4.1 million barrels in the same period last year.
Markets would be inactive, with liquidity sapped by a regional supply conference on Monday and Tuesday, traders said.
++ Diesel. May CARB diesel fuel rose 1.50 cents a gallon Friday to 54.50/55.50 cents.
